summary: The root H-L-L primarily signifies appearing, shining, or becoming visible, like the new moon. It also conveys the idea of beginning something, especially a new month.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: أَهْلَلْنَا هِلَالَ شَهْرِ كَذَا : see سَلَخَ .

parts.t: : see a verse cited at the close of the first paragraph of art.
. See also a verse cited voce

headwords.def: اِسْتَهَلَّ : see a verse cited at the close of the first paragraph of art. ضحك . See also a verse cited voce أَفْثَأَ . See مُسْتَهَلٌّ .

هَلْ may be originally هَلْو or هَلْى or هَلّ : (Akh, in S, voce بل :) see بَلْ . هَلْ followed by إِلَى : see the latter. حَىّ هَلَ : see حى . هَلَّا : see حَضَّةٌ and عَنْ , latter part, and لَوْلَا , and أَلَّا .

headwords.gloss: The new moon; the moon when it is termed; the moon when near the sun

headwords.def: الهِلاَلُ The new moon; or the moon when it is termed هِلاَل : it may be explained as meaning, generally, the moon when near the sun, or moon a little after or before the change. See سَمَا .

headwords.gloss: The first night of the lunar month

parts.t: The first night of the lunar month.

headwords.def: مُسْتَهَلُّ الشَّهْرِ The first night of the lunar month. (Msb.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
